B2B SAASPOSITIONING / WEBSITE

Repositioning Freight Tiger as India's AI-native freight operating system

My role Led positioning, messaging and content for the new freighttiger.com and tigersight.ai. Guided the designers and wrote the About Us page.

The new homepage, live at freighttiger.com: one category claim, scale proof, and one connected system.

“The site undersold a company that had outgrown it. Freight Tiger had moved from visibility to a full TMS, a two-sided marketplace, and an AI layer, but a visitor couldn't say in one line what it actually was, a tracking tool, a TMS, a load board, or an AI company, and TigerSight, the newest and most strategic product, had no clear home.”

The positioning
The category claim every page ladders up to

India's AI-native freight operating system

One company, one line. Underneath it, four layers, and each one gets exactly one job and one primary buyer.

Freight TigerThe operating system
Run every freight movement with one connected system
Primary buyerEnterprise leadership
TMSThe execution backbone
One TMS, from plan to payment
Primary buyerLogistics & supply chain heads
MarketplaceThe capacity network
Place every load faster, keep every truck moving
Primary buyerLSPs & fleet owners
TigerSightThe intelligence layer
Turn live freight data into decisions and action
Primary buyerShippers, procurement, CXOs
Before and after
Before

“All Movement. No Chaos.” Legacy nav split across FT Visibility, FT TMS, and separate shipper/LSP menus, with no single category claim.

After

“Run every freight movement with one connected system.” The category is named above the headline and the nav follows the four layers.

Before

The old “Our Solutions” page: three modules (Visibility, TMS, Procurement) competing side by side with no hierarchy.

After

“One TMS. From plan to payment.” One product, one job, told as Plan, Procure, Execute, Settle.

After

Inside the page, each capability states what it does and the three outcomes it delivers, in the same pattern every time.

Taking the positioning into the boardroom

The same architecture became the spine of Freight Tiger’s enterprise and strategic-partner narrative. The story moved up a level, from “freight software” to “India’s digital freight infrastructure, powered by software, AI and network intelligence”, told as three connected layers with the company’s scale and its three-chapter history as proof.

The opportunity, framed as three connected layers: workflows (TMS), network (Marketplace) and intelligence (TigerSight AI), each with its own product proof.

Credibility before capability: scale, enterprise logos, and the same visible → operating infrastructure → intelligent arc written for the About Us page.

How the positioning carried through
01

Stopped selling modules, sold one connected system

Built a four-layer architecture instead of a feature list, Freight Tiger as the operating system, the TMS as the execution backbone, the Marketplace as the capacity network, TigerSight as the intelligence layer, each with one job and one primary buyer.

02

Built the homepage as a single argument, top to bottom

Structured it to read as one case rather than a catalogue: hero category claim, scale proof (5% of India's FTL freight, 18M+ trips a year, 400+ enterprise shippers), industry fit, CFO-level outcomes, and a consultative CTA offering a demo, a call, a supply chain consultation, or proof of ROI, instead of one generic 'book a demo' button.

03

Gave three very different audiences three different paths

The Marketplace page alone speaks to two opposite buyers, LSPs and fleet owners, through self-selecting entry points and parallel five-step journeys, rather than one blended pitch trying to serve both.

04

Wrote the company's origin story end to end

Authored the About Us page as a three-chapter arc, making freight visible (2017-20), building the operating infrastructure (2021-24), making the network intelligent (2025 onward), so TigerSight reads as the natural next chapter, not a pivot.

05

Turned the positioning into the strategic-partner pitch

Rebuilt the enterprise narrative on the same architecture: the opportunity as “from digitising freight to intelligent infrastructure”, three connected layers instead of a product list, scale and the origin arc as proof, measured customer outcomes by industry, and a growth story of multimodal India plus AI-native products for global markets.

Outcome
1
Category story replacing three competing product pitches, carried from five core web pages into enterprise and strategic-partner pitches
4
Product layers, each with exactly one job and one primary buyer
3
Audiences, shippers, LSPs, and fleet owners, given their own messaging and conversion paths for the first time
2
